html:
Joseph II was Holy Roman Emperor from 1765 and sole ruler of the Habsburg lands from 1780 to 1790, after his mother Maria Theresa. He is the classic example of an enlightened despot.

Inspired by the Enlightenment, he issued thousands of decrees. He gave toleration to Protestants, Orthodox Christians and Jews, abolished serfdom in 1781, closed hundreds of monasteries, ended censorship of much writing, and made German the language of government. He opened the great general hospital of Vienna and the Prater park to the public.

He moved too fast. Hungarians and the people of the Austrian Netherlands revolted, and he had to withdraw many reforms before he died. He was a patron of Mozart. See Austria.
sum: Joseph II was Holy Roman Emperor from 1765 and sole ruler of the Habsburg lands from 1780 to 1790, after his mother Maria Theresa. He is the classic example of an enlightened despot.
